subject.title: [Regression]: sessions_spawn missing scope operator.write — introduced between v2026.6.1 and v2026.6.11

question: Should in-process `callSubagentGateway({ method: "agent" })` use a synthetic `operator.write` client after `sessions_spawn` tool policy has allowed the spawn?
rationale: Current source shows the bug path, but the linked fix deliberately changes the internal authorization boundary and that intent should be confirmed by a maintainer before landing.

options.title: Confirm Synthetic Write Boundary
options.body: Land the linked narrow fix after redacted token-auth channel proof confirms `sessions_spawn` succeeds and admin cleanup remains admin-scoped.

options.title: Require Device-Identity Fix Instead
options.body: Reject the synthetic-client approach and require a fix in Gateway device identity or credential resolution if maintainers want the caller identity preserved.

options.title: Pause For Broader Auth Cluster
options.body: Hold this issue behind the broader token-auth/operator-scope cluster if maintainers want one canonical auth repair for related reports.

recommendation.title: Confirm Synthetic Write Boundary
recommendation.body: Land the linked narrow fix after redacted token-auth channel proof confirms `sessions_spawn` succeeds and admin cleanup remains admin-scoped.
